summary: This Dockerfile sets up a Node.js container with Chromium, fonts, and Python support for running Mermaid diagram generation. It installs system dependencies needed for headless browser automation, configures Puppeteer to use the pre-installed Chromium, and prepares the environment for the application.

explanations.3: The --no-cache flag tells Alpine's package manager to skip caching packages, which saves space in the Docker image since we don't need to reinstall them later.
explanations.15: This command rebuilds the font cache so the system recognizes all the fonts we just installed, making them available to Chromium and other tools.
explanations.19: We're creating a directory where Puppeteer (the headless browser library) will cache data, and making it world-writable so the node user can access it.
explanations.22: This tells Puppeteer not to download its own copy of Chromium, since we're providing one via the system package manager instead.
explanations.23: This explicitly points Puppeteer to the Chromium binary we installed in line 4, so it knows exactly where to find the browser executable.
